skill.name: flow-nexus-swarm
skill.description: Deploy and manage Flow Nexus cloud swarms, workflows, message queues, and agent coordination from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.
skill.summary: Orchestrate cloud AI agent swarms and event-driven workflows with Flow Nexus.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: The static Ruby and shell backtick findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences and inline code examples. I found one semantic issue: the skill instructs users to install and run remote npm or npx packages and add a Flow Nexus MCP server, which creates supply-chain and third-party execution risk.

remediation.issue: Remote package installation and MCP server startup
remediation.suggestion: Pin exact package versions or integrity hashes, document trust boundaries, and require confirmation before running npm, npx, or MCP server commands.
Replace floating tags with vetted versions and update them through release notes or a signed release process.

remediation.issue: Cloud service data handling is not described
remediation.suggestion: Explain what task data is sent to Flow Nexus, how it is retained, and how users can limit sensitive inputs.

static_findings.snippet: - **Parallel Execution**: Set `parallel: true` for concurrent steps

semantic_findings.title: External Package Execution Instructions
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells users to run npx claude-flow@alpha hooks and to install or run flow-nexus@latest commands, then add an MCP server. These floating package executions create supply-chain and third-party code execution risk if followed without review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines directly show npm, npx, and claude mcp commands using @alpha or @latest. The risk is supply-chain exposure, not evidence of malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Distributed AI work is hard to coordinate across agents, workflows, and queues. This skill guides Flow Nexus swarm setup, task routing, monitoring, templates, and cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Initialize Flow Nexus swarms with hierarchical, mesh, ring, or star topology.
Spawn named agents with roles such as researcher, coder, analyst, optimizer, or coordinator.
Create and execute event-driven workflows with dependencies, triggers, retries, and async queue processing.
Monitor swarm status, workflow status, queue status, audit trails, and execution streams.
Use documented templates for development, research, CI/CD, data pipelines, security audits, and enterprise workflows.
limitations: Requires a Flow Nexus account and the Flow Nexus MCP server.
May run cloud workflows that send task data to an external service.
Does not verify package integrity for the documented npm and npx commands.
Examples are operational guidance, not a complete application or deployment policy.

use_cases.title: Automate Release Workflows
use_cases.description: Create CI/CD workflows with test, build, scan, deploy, rollback, and audit steps.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Multi-Agent Delivery
use_cases.description: Assign specialized agents to research, backend, frontend, database, integration, and QA work.

use_cases.title: Run Data Processing Pipelines
use_cases.description: Model ETL workflows with validation, transformation, enrichment, loading, retry policy, and scheduled triggers.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Swarm
prompt_templates.prompt: Use flow-nexus-swarm to initialize a hierarchical swarm for a small web application. Spawn coordinator, coder, analyst, and optimizer agents.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use flow-nexus-swarm to design an event-driven workflow for testing, building, security scanning, staging deployment, and production deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Monitor and Tune
prompt_templates.prompt: Use flow-nexus-swarm to review workflow status, queue health, audit trail, and swarm metrics. Recommend scaling and cleanup actions.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Multi-Phase Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Use flow-nexus-swarm to plan research, development, testing, and release swarms for a multi-repository migration. Include dependencies and failure handling.

output_examples.input: Plan a swarm for a full-stack project.
output: Recommends hierarchical topology with six agents.
Assigns coordinator, backend, frontend, database, QA, and optimizer roles.
Defines workflow stages from requirements through testing.
Summarizes workflow status, queue depth, failed steps, and recent audit events.
Highlights scaling opportunities and cleanup actions.
Separates operational issues from configuration changes.
Outlines extraction, validation, transformation, enrichment, load, and final validation stages.
Includes retry policy, scheduling, and monitoring guidance.
Names the agent responsibilities for each stage.

best_practices: Confirm the Flow Nexus account, project scope, and data sensitivity before running cloud workflows.
Use pinned package versions and reviewed MCP server configuration in production environments.
Destroy unused swarms and review audit trails after each workflow execution.
anti_patterns: Running npm or npx commands from the skill without checking package source and version.
Sending secrets, customer data, or private repository content into cloud workflows without approval.
Leaving experimental swarms active after the task is complete.

faq.question: Does this skill require external services?
faq.answer: Yes. It depends on Flow Nexus cloud infrastructure and an active Flow Nexus account.

faq.question: Can it run local-only swarms?
faq.answer: The documented focus is Flow Nexus cloud orchestration. Local coordination is directed to Claude Flow.

faq.question: What tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: The skill file is documentation. Users still choose whether to run the shown MCP and npm commands.

faq.question: What data should users avoid sending?
faq.answer: Avoid secrets, regulated data, and private source content unless your organization approves the Flow Nexus workflow.

faq.question: How should teams use it safely?
faq.answer: Pin versions, review MCP configuration, limit sensitive input, monitor audit trails, and clean up swarms.
